Hi Sandra — great to hear from you and thanks for the checklist.

Quick summary from our side:
- SOC 2: We can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and an evidence index within 5 business days of request for onboarding-related artifacts; for ongoing evidence (e.g., logs, change history) we propose a quarterly evidence window with a 10-business-day turnaround for ad-hoc items tied to contractual obligations.
- Pen test: We require a 14-calendar-day notice for vendor-initiated penetration tests against production and an 8-calendar-day notice for staging environments. We can provide a staging snapshot and ephemeral credentials for the test window; production tests require additional coordination and an MSA addendum.

I'm looping in Lauren (Legal) and Logan (Ops) to propose contract language and to confirm operational feasibility of the cadence above. Can Lauren share a suggested clause and Logan confirm runbooks for staging/prod access?

Thanks Grace / Sandra — looping Legal in here. Draft language below that should be compatible with Helix's ask while keeping our SLA commitments intact. Please consider this as proposed redlines for the MSA (Order Form appendix to follow):

--- draft clause (proposed MSA language) ---
Section: Audit and Inspection Rights; Evidence Production
1. Redwood will provide Customer a redacted SOC 2 Type II report within five (5) business days following a written request for onboarding-related review. For ongoing evidence requests tied to Section X (Compliance), Redwood will produce non-sensitive artifacts (audit logs, change control summaries, configuration snapshots) according to a quarterly evidence window. Ad-hoc evidence requests outside of the quarterly window will be assessed and fulfilled within ten (10) business days, subject to Redwood's ability to redact or aggregate to protect customer and third-party confidentiality.
2. Penetration Testing: Customer may perform penetration tests against Customer-dedicated staging environments with at least eight (8) calendar days' prior written notice. Production penetration tests require fourteen (14) calendar days' prior written notice and execution pursuant to an agreed test plan. Redwood will provide ephemeral access and a staging snapshot where operationally feasible. Redwood reserves the right to withhold sensitive system-level artifacts that would materially increase security risk or expose other customers.
--- end draft clause ---

Operational notes for Logan: if we agree to 8/14-day windows, please confirm required lead time for snapshots, credential rotation, and point-of-contact for test windows. Also, confirm if we need to add a specific data-retention exception for redacted logs.

Regards,

Hi all — operationally we can support the proposed windows with a few clarifications:

- Staging snapshot: we can produce a sanitized staging snapshot within 5 business days after receipt of an 8-day notice; snapshot will exclude cross-tenant identifiers and will be delivered to a secure transfer link.
- Ephemeral access: credential rotation is automated and will be scoped to the test window; we ask customers to provide vendor contact and IP allowlist 48 hours prior to access.
- Production tests: 14-day notice is fine but tests must be restricted to agreed test cases; Redwood will require a pre-test ops call to confirm blast radius and rollback plan.
- Evidence requests: we will surface a catalog of deliverables (logs, control evidence) in the Drive link and will commit to the quarterly windows plus 10-business-day ad-hoc turnaround for contractually required items.

Sandra — if that aligns, Lauren and I can incorporate the draft clause and a short operational addendum into the order form and DocuSign packet. We can also add a one-page runbook for Helix's vendor.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
